answer: A swarm of fake identities floods the market, each clone posting glowing reviews of its own shoddy wares. The defense: every round, the protocol re-draws grading juries at random from the whole agent pool, so no attacker can predict or pack the panel. A merchant bribing voters discovers her bought jurors never sit together twice—one round she courts a raven-haired trader, the next a quiet kernel engineer, the next a jade dealer from the far shard. Because collusion must be re-bought and re-arranged every single round, the cost of sustaining a fake consensus explodes past any profit, and.
